memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They had not gone far from the city when Joseph said to his steward, 'Go after those men at once, and when you catch up with them, say to them, "Why have you repaid good with evil?"'" — Gen 44:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Why have you repaid good with evil?" It is a piercing question, and Joseph knows exactly what he is doing when he tells his steward to ask it. The brothers are innocent of the cup. But they are not innocent of that question. Twenty years earlier, they had repaid a father's love and a brother's obedience with betrayal and a pit.

God has a way of bringing old, buried things back to the surface. Not to torment us, but because unconfessed sin does not simply fade away with time. It waits. And a merciful God will often arrange the circumstances that force it into the open — because what is hidden cannot be healed.

Joseph is not being cruel here. He is doing surgery. The wound in this family has been covered over for two decades, and it has never healed underneath. Now it must be opened.

If God has been pressing on an old area of your life — a relationship you damaged, a wrong you never made right, something you have hoped everyone forgot — that pressure is not condemnation. It is grace. He brings it up because He intends to deal with it fully in Christ, where it can be truly forgiven and finally put down (1 Jn 1:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something buried in your past that God keeps gently bringing back to mind?
2. Why is it so tempting to hope that time alone will heal what only confession can heal?
3. Where have you repaid someone's kindness with unkindness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see the things I have covered over and hoped to forget. Bring them into Your light, not to shame me, but so that I can confess them and be truly free. Amen.
